instruction.text: These two medieval peasants are having a conversation. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Hello, John! That’s a lot of ((++vegetables violins)). Where are you going today?
atoms.sound: Hello John! That’s a lot of vegetables. Where are you going today?

atoms.b: Hi, Geoffrey! My farm has produced a lot of extra food this year, so I am taking it to the ((++market moon)).
atoms.sound: Hi Geoffrey! My farm has produced a lot of extra food this year, so I am taking it to the market.

atoms.b: The market? That’s in the next ((++town tree))! How are you getting there?
I will have my donkey pull my ((++wagon watermelon)). It is a long journey.
Wow! I’ve never been that far out of the ((++village villain))! You’re very lucky you own a ((++donkey dodo))!

instruction.text: Which three things do you think would have made John’s journey difficult?

feedback.end: In the past, travelling could be dangerous and took a very long time. Luckily, modern technology has made it much easier.

instruction.text: Select the correct form of medieval travel

feedback.correct: Carriages were very expensive and needed you to employ a driver, so only the very rich nobility could afford them.
Because horses were expensive, most people who owned them were also quite wealthy, like knights.
Most people had neither a carriage nor a horse, so they had to walk everywhere.

atoms.a: In the past, people did not travel outside their villages often.
The roads were often bad for travel.
Means of transport were much faster than todays.
